# Living Sun · Earth · Moon

> A playful toy, not a scientific tool. It is built on real data — the Sun, Earth and Moon in their true positions for the current moment, live satellite clouds and local weather — and mixes it with pure fun: click any place on Earth to open a sky window with stars, sounds, rhinos, elephants, toads, bats and a dancing, laughing clown.

Site: https://sun-earth-moon-webgpu.pages.dev/

## What it shows

- The Sun with an animated surface, corona and prominences; the Earth with day/night, city lights and live satellite clouds; the Moon with real phase.
- Positions of the Sun, Moon and Earth are computed for the current date and time (Astronomy Engine).
- Clicking a point on Earth opens the sky above it right now: the Sun and Moon at their real altitude and azimuth, stars and the 88 IAU constellations, cloud cover by layer and wind from Open-Meteo, and the nearest town (GeoNames).
- On land: grass, rhinos, elephants, toads, bats at dusk and a dancing clown; over water: waves and a jumping mackerel. Animals react to clicks with sounds.

## How to use

- Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, double-click the Sun, Earth or Moon to fly to it.
- Click the Earth to open the sky window; drag inside it to look around, scroll to zoom; buttons for Sun, Moon, sound, flashlight and full screen.
- Parameters panel: time speed, Earth–Sun distance, real scale, "Now", "Where am I", rendering quality (Auto / High / Medium / Low / Lowest).

## Requirements

- A browser with WebGPU support (recent Chrome, Edge, Arc, Safari 26+). A capable GPU gives the best result; quality adapts automatically on weaker systems.

## Data and privacy

- No accounts, no cookies. Anonymous page-view statistics are counted by Cloudflare Web Analytics.
- The visitor's position stays in the browser; only the coordinates of a selected point are sent to Open-Meteo for weather; clicking a constellation requests its description from Wikipedia.

## Credits

- Full list of models, sounds, textures, data sources and libraries with licenses is in the "Credits" dialog on the page.
